title: Ask Anything AI
summary: A generic chat box that forwards user text to a hosted language model.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: The team wanted an AI feature for the hackathon.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: No non-AI alternative or bounded user problem was evaluated.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Use a generic hosted-model chat call.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Responses can be wrong and the interface does not distinguish uncertainty.
design_decisions.validation_approach: The author manually asked two questions.

testing_strategy: There are no automated tests or documented evaluation cases.
security_threat: User text may include sensitive data and responses may be misleading. A disclaimer says AI can make mistakes. Residual risk: No retention policy, redaction, output constraints, abuse handling, or evaluation evidence exists.
production_limitation: Accuracy, latency, cost, safety, and user benefit are unknown.
technical_debt: Define a real user problem, data policy, evaluation set, uncertainty behavior, and non-AI baseline.
track_alignment_explanation: The submission calls this Human-Scale AI, but it is a generic wrapper without a bounded context, demonstrated necessity, or deliberate human-agency design.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
